text:
alex: heads up — seeing NVMe io_queue_depth climbing on eu-central ephemerals for the last 12m. cleaner jobs are moving to "deferred" state frequently and we're getting a small spike in gpu attach failures (approx 5% of attempts).

alex: stack trace-ish from node gnode-euc-412:```INFO cleaner: deferred eviction window start=2026-03-21T09:12:03Z reason=io_pressure backlog=1840 io_qd=256
WARN nvme: write retries x12, rc=EIO
```

priya: thanks — is this correlated with any batch job burst or scrub schedule?

alex: looks like nightly scrub overlapped with a large RL batch surge ~09:05-09:18. scrub cadence was 09:00 as usual; cleaner concurrency dropped from 8 -> 2 after the deferrals.

marc: @alex can you dump cleaner pod logs and the cleaner metrics? Also run `kubectl get pods -l app=ephemeral-cleaner -n infra -o wide`

alex: ran it, output snippet:```NAME                              READY STATUS   RESTARTS   AGE
ephemeral-cleaner-0               1/1   Running   0          15h
ephemeral-cleaner-1               0/1   CrashLoop 5          3m
metrics: cleaner_active_workers=2 cleaner_deferred_count=128 nvme_write_lat_p95=420ms
```

infra-bot: [alert] nvme_io_pressure_high on eu-central region — threshold crossed: io_qd>200. Incident: #INC-20260321-01 created.

sasha: quick take — when cleaner defers it leaves lots of small deletes queued which increases read-modify-write churn on NVMe. This can blow up iops for small-block workloads. If GPUs are trying to attach and format volumes at same time, attach latency + IO retries = attach failures.

priya: mitigation options: 1) temporarily pause non-critical scrubs in eu-central, 2) increase cleaner concurrency/priority, 3) throttle RL batch batcher for 15m, or 4) move some attaches to dedicated capacity. Thoughts?

marc: prefer 1+2 initially. Pausing scrubs is low-risk for 15-30m and we can bump cleaner concurrency to 6. I'll push a canary change to conflist: `PATCH /infra/cleaner/config concurrency=6 region=eu-central`

alex: will follow with the `kubectl scale` if you push the config. Also starting a temporary QOS rule to deprioritize small-block deletes for RL batch:```tc qdisc add dev nvme0 root tbf rate 400mbit burst 32k latency 50ms```

marc: config applied (canary). scaling cleaner pods now.

alex: scaled cleaner replicas 2 -> 6, monitoring. nvme_io_qd dropping: 256 -> 108 in 90s. attach failures down to 1.2%.

sasha: nice. follow-up items: - add backpressure-aware scrub scheduling (avoid scrub start in same 30m window as large batch launches) - add a guard to cleaner that refuses to move to deferred if backlog > X without raising a higher-severity alert - update runbooks.

priya: agreed. I'll open a short RFC for scrub scheduling changes and add the guard to the cleaner backlog heuristics. For now we keep throttles for 10m and monitor. :thumbsup:

alex: leaving the temporary tc rule in place for 5m then remove. nvme_qd stable ~95. If anything regresses ping me.

infra-bot: [resolve] nvme_io_pressure_high on eu-central cleared at 2026-03-21T09:23:20Z. Incident closed.
